title.value: Temporal Profiles of Social Attention Are Different Across Development in Autistic and Neurotypical People
title.justification: The title of the paper is "Temporal Profiles of Social Attention Are Different Across Development in Autistic and Neurotypical People." This is explicitly stated in the header of the document.
title.quote: Temporal Profiles of Social Attention Are Different Across Development in Autistic and Neurotypical People

analysis.description: The paper investigates the differences in social attention temporal profiles between autistic and neurotypical individuals across age ranges, using eye-tracking data and growth curve analysis on a large sample. It highlights developmental differences in social attention dynamics and their associations with communicative skills in autistic individuals.

type.justification: The study is empirical as it involves data collection and analysis from eye-tracking experiments with autistic and neurotypical participants to understand differences in social attention.
type.quote: METHODS: We used growth curve analysis to model attention to static social scenes as a function of time in a large (N = 650) sample of autistic participants and neurotypical participants across a wide age range (6–30 years).

name.justification: The primary research field is developmental psychology, focusing on the temporal dynamics of social attention in autistic versus neurotypical individuals, which is a topic within developmental studies.
name.quote: These findings show that social attention not only is reduced in ASD, but also differs in its temporal dynamics. The neurotypical participants became more sophisticated in how they deployed their social attention across age, a pattern that was significantly reduced in the participants with ASD.

name.justification: The research is heavily focused on autism, examining differences in social attention between those with autism spectrum disorder and neurotypical individuals.
name.quote: Sociocommunicative difficulties, including abnormalities in eye contact, are core diagnostic features of autism spectrum disorder (ASD).

name.justification: The paper focuses on the dynamic patterns of social attention among autistic and neurotypical individuals.
name.quote: The neurotypical participants became more sophisticated in how they deployed their social attention across age, a pattern that was significantly reduced in the participants with ASD, possibly reflecting delayed acquisition of social expertise.

name.justification: The paper uses eye-tracking data from the EU-AIMS Longitudinal European Autism Project for its analysis.
name.quote: We used the eye-tracking data from the multisite EU-AIMS LEAP (European Autism Interventions Longitudinal European Autism Project) study (29).
